public_rationale: Contemporaneous technical sources describe hallucination as an unresolved problem. GPT-4 still hallucinated, a November review identified continuing problems across LLMs, and verification research reported reductions rather than elimination. This supports the historical observation. It does not establish that a new paradigm is necessary; Marcus presented that possibility as uncertain.
limitations: Support concerns a general solution, not whether particular applications could achieve useful reliability.
A literature review cannot prove the absence of every unpublished method.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The hallucination problem has never been solved and may not be until a new paradigm is found.
conditions: possibly not until a new paradigm

statement.excerpt: There has never been a solution to the hallucination problem, and it’s not clear that there will be until we find a new paradigm, as Altman himself partly acknowledged last week, when he did his best Gary Marcus impression.
statement.document_title: Top 5 reasons why OpenAI was probably never really worth $86 billion

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that no generally effective solution to factual hallucinations in open-ended LLM generation had been demonstrated by publication.
Reducing hallucinations, or preventing them in a restricted task, does not establish a general solution.
The statement about a possible new paradigm expresses uncertainty. It is not a firm forecast that a new paradigm is necessary.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous research reviews and model evaluations identify hallucinations as an unresolved general problem despite available mitigation methods.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A method publicly demonstrated by November 22, 2023 reliably eliminated factual hallucinations across open-ended LLM uses.

evidence.excerpt: Most importantly, it still is not fully reliable (it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors).
evidence.explanation: OpenAI acknowledged residual factual hallucinations in GPT-4. The surrounding discussion reports improvements, not elimination.

evidence.excerpt: Nevertheless, alongside these strides, LLMs exhibit a critical tendency to produce hallucinations, resulting in content that is inconsistent with real-world facts or user inputs.
evidence.explanation: This review describes hallucination as a continuing problem across LLMs shortly before the post. It reviews mitigation methods and remaining limitations.

evidence.excerpt: Generation of plausible yet incorrect factual information, termed hallucination, is an unsolved issue in large language models.
evidence.explanation: The authors explicitly call the problem unsolved while reporting reductions through verification. Those improvements qualify any suggestion that progress required a new paradigm, but do not contradict the historical observation.
